newsitem.title: UK: Major says UK voters won't trust Labour on economy.
newsitem.headline: Major says UK voters won't trust Labour on economy.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said he did not believe voters would reject a Conservative government which had produced "sparkling economic prospects" in favour of a Labour administration in the general election.
"People can now see that the action we took on the economy has worked," he said in an interview with BBC Radio Four.

"We now have the best economy of any country in western Europe, not just this year, but...next year and the year after that. Can people see that? They can. Will they want to throw it away? They will not."
Major said voters still did not know the details of Labour policy.

"They do know that Labour's policies invariably lead to higher unemployment, higher taxes, higher mortgage rates and an economy that underperforms. I do not believe people will make that option their choice in the general election," he added.
Major, who lost his majority in parliament last month, must call a general election by May 22.
Asked about Labour's strong lead in opinion polls, he replied: "I was miles behind in the opinion polls four days before the last general election and I won it by seven percent."
